JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a Road Traffic accident.
2. Brief case of the petitioner in the nutshell:

It is the case of the petitioner that, on 16.06.2023 at about 11.30 a.m, the deceased was proceeding on his Honda Activa scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-05-KC-5820 from NCB Circle to K.R. Circle and when he reached near Lakshmi Venkateshwara Temple, SCCH-23 MVC-6295/2023 Karisandra, BSK 2nd Stage, Bengaluru City and while taking U turn by observing all the traffic rules and regulations at that time, a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-JW-5490 came in rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and dashed to the rear side of the deceased's motorcycle.

As a result of impact the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries and soon after the accident he was shifted to Excel Care Hospital, Bengaluru and then he was shifted to St.John's Hospital, Bengaluru
. During the course of treatment he succumbed to the injuries on 17.06.2023.
It is submitted that postmortem was conducted and corpse was handed over to the family members.
It is further submitted that because of death of deceased the petitioner has suffered both financially and emotionally.
Further the petitioner has spent substantial amount towards medical expenses, transportation of dead body and funeral obsequies.
It is submitted that, prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy, he was doing consultant and also real estate agent and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- p.m.

It is contended that the accident happened because of rash and negligent riding of the rider of the SCCH-23 MVC-6295/2023 motorcycle and as such both the respondents No.1 to 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence prayed to allow the petition.
3. Summons was duly served to respondent No.1 & 2, the respondent No.1 & 2 did not appear before this Tribunal.
Hence they were placed exparte.

4. After service of notice, the respondent No.3 spurred in rush to the Court by filing written statement rather objections to the petition contending that the petition is not maintainable either law or on facts.
The respondent No.3 admitting the issuance of insurance policy in respect of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-JW-5490.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
Non- compliance of section's 147, 149, 134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act is pleaded.
Further the petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Negligence on the part of the rider of its insured vehicle is denied by this SCCH-23 MVC-6295/2023 respondent.

Per contra it is alleged that, the unfortunate accident happened only due to the negligent riding of the deceased himself in the middle of the road and at the time of riding the motorcycle the deceased was not wearing helmet and he was also not Lalithamma vs Gulab Khan on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175369979/
2 having valid DL at the time of accident.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the rider of the insured vehicle did not possess valid & effective DL.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that she is the legal heir and dependent of the deceased ?
2) Whether the petitioner proves

that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 16.06.2023 at about 11.30 a.m.,
near Lakshmi Venkateshwar Temple, SCCH-23 MVC-6295/2023 Karisandra,
Banashankari 2nd Stage, Bengaluru City, due to actionable negligence of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-JW-5490 ?
3) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed?

If so, at what rate and from whom ?
4) What order or award ?
6. Petitioner No.1 examined herself as PW.1.
Ex's .
P1 to 19 were marked on behalf of the petitioners.
The respondents have not choose to lead evidence.
7. Heard erudite counsel for the petitioners and respondents counsel on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

8. This tribunal answers to the above issues are as follows :-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per final order for the  following :
 REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.2 : The petitioner has knocked the doors of justice with a relief to grant a compensation of an amount to SCCH-23 MVC-6295/2023 the tune of Rs.15,00,000/- together.

The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint lodged by son of the deceased by name Sri. John Santhosh herein, the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed Lalithamma vs Gulab Khan on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175369979/
3 charge sheet against the rider of the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-JW- 5490 for the offences punishable under section's 279, 304(A) of IPC and u/s 134(A&B), 187 of IMV Act.
10.
In order to prove the facum of negligence the petitioner has mainly relied on Ex.P.1 to 14 documents being the police documents.
Negligence has to be proved as a matter of fact.

Added more with regard to the cause of death, Postmortem was conducted as per Ex.P.12 wherein it reflects that the cause of death is was due to skull fracture and intracranial hemorrhage as a result of head injury sustained.
The only dispute in controversy is with regard to the negligence.
It is relevant to note that Ex.P.14 charge sheet is filed as against the rider of offending motorcycle.

It is vociferously urged by the respondent No.2 counsel that, there is a negligence on the part of the SCCH-23 MVC-6295/2023 deceased himself was riding the motorcycle without observing vehicular movements.
11. Further more on perusal of Ex.P.6 and 7 being the Spot Mahazar and Sketch prepared at the time of drawing spot mahazar.
Further the spot mahzar and sketch it reflects that the accident happened on NCB Circle towards to K.R. Road, Bengaluru City near Karisandra, BSK 2 nd Stage, Bengaluru.
On close perusal of the same it reflects that, the motorcycle in which the deceased was traveling was hit by the motorcycle to its right rear side.
Further the contents of the Ex.P.6 & 7, wherein it shows that the width of the said road is 30 feets and it was two way road.
It is further shows that the accident occured on the extreme side of the road.
The rider of the offending motorcycle came from same direction and dashed the deceased's motorcycle from right hind side.
On close perusal of the Ex.P13/IMV Report it reflects the rear side of the deceased scooter is damaged.

This categorically reflects that the offending motorcycle had hit the vehicle of the deceased's from hind side shows that there is a negligence on the part of the rider of the SCCH-23 MVC-6295/2023 offending motorcycle.
If the rider of the offending motorcycle was coming in a normal speed then he would certainly avoided the accident.

The IMV report which is read in consonance with the spot mahazar and sketch and in the light of charge sheet it is crystal clear that the offending motorcycle had hit the scooter of the deceased from its hind side.

Above all even the charge sheet was also filed as against the rider of the motorcycle for the offences punishable u/s 279 and 304A of IPC.
12.
The Learned counsel for respondent No.2 argued that deceased was not wearing helmet and he has contributed for negligence.

In order to controvert the above said contention, the it is relevant to relied on the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Civil Appeal No.79/2020 (Mohammad Siddique & another V/s National Insurance Company Ltd & others), wherein it is held that "Simply because there is a violation of Section 129 of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988 by a victim in an accident,
there is no presumption that there is contributory negligence on the part of the person who was not wearing the helmet.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is to be decided in the facts and SCCH-23 MVC-6295/2023 circumstances of each case".
That is to say, some other additional evidence is necessary to attribute contributory negligence to the deceased which is not adduced in this case.
All the mist of doubt created by the respondent No.2 during the course of trail is demystified by the petitioner.

Added more further it is also relevant to rely on the Judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Dharwad Bench in MFA.101144/2020 (MV-I) in the case of Anand v/s Arjun and The Oriental Ins.Co.Ltd., wherein also the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, had interpreted Sec.129 of IMV Act had also held that non wearing of helmet is not a ground to deny the compensation.

sentences.text: It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others SCCH-23 MVC-6295/2023 which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs.
Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105, where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the rider of the offending van.

sentences.text: Even in the instant case the rider of the motorcycle is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part and even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred SCCH-23 MVC-6295/2023 only due to the fault of the rider of the motorcycle and he was charge sheeted.
Another important aspects to be noted here is, respondent No.2 did not made any endevour to examine the rider of the insured motorcycle.

Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side,
which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Under such circumstances the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the rider of the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-JW-5490.
As such, this Tribunal answers issue No.2 In the Affirmative.
14. ISSUE NO.1:
The petitioner claim that, petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased.
To prove the same, petitioner No.1 filed affidavit-in-lieu of her chief-examination and deposed about the above relationship.
The Aadhaar cards, DL and PAN card of petitioners and deceased and contents of the police papers do fortify the said fact.
It is pertinent to note that, this relationship of the petitioner with the deceased was not disputed by the respondents.

Since the evidence led by the SCCH-23 MVC-6295/2023 petitioner is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioner is the legal representative of the deceased.
Therefore, petitioner is the legal heir and dependent of deceased.
Hence, this Tribunal answers to issue No.1 In the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE NO.3:
In this case the petitioner has claimed the compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- on the death of deceased in the road traffic accident.
The petitioner contended that, deceased was working as consultant and real estate agent and earning of Rs.25,000/-p.m.
To prove the income of the deceased, the petitioner has not produced any documents.
16. Be that as it may, in the absence of authentic proof of income of the deceased, this Tribunal has to consider his income notionally for calculating the compensation.
Admittedly the accident took place in the year 2023.
It is trite law that, when the petitioners have failed to prove the income, the income of the deceased has to be taken into consideration as notional income.

It is relevant to rely Lalithamma vs Gulab Khan on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175369979/
5 on the decision of Hon'ble SCCH-23 MVC-6295/2023 High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV)
dated.05.07.2023.

entities.text: SCCH-23 MVC-6295/2023 High Court of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred on 16.06.2023.

Therefore, Rs.16,000/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the deceased.
SCCH-23 MVC-6295/2023 17.

So far as the age of the deceased is concerned, the petitioner has produced the DL and PAN card of the deceased as per Ex.P.15 & 17, wherein, the date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 04.01.1953 and the accident had taken place on 16.06.2023 and it shows that, at the time of accident the deceased was aged about 70 years 5 months 12 days.

Hence the proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is '5'.
18.
In the case on hand the deceased was aged 70 years.
His income is taken as Rs.16,000/- p.m.
As per dictum of Hon'ble Apex Court in AIR 2017 SC 5157, the deceased is not entitled to future prospects (as he was aged more than 60 years).
The deceased died living behind one dependent.

As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma Case, 1/3rd of his income is required to be deducted towards his personal expenses which comes to Rs.10,667/- p.m. (Rs.16,000 - Rs.5,333 = Rs.10,667/-).
19. The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.10,667/- p.m. and the multiplier '5' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.6,40,020/- (Rs.10,667 X 12 X 5).
Considering the SCCH-23 MVC-6295/2023 above facts, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.6,40,000/- under the head of loss of dependency.

20. Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to estate, funeral expenses and consortium is to be awarded.

6

Hence this Tribunal award Rs.18,150/- towards loss to estate and Rs.18,150/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years and Rs.48,400/- towards consortium to the petitioner No.1.
By applying the observations made in the aforesaid case, as more than 6 years elapsed from the date of order amount of consortium, funeral expense and loss of estate to be enhanced.
21. MEDICAL EXPENSES : 2-Medical bills produced by PW.1 are marked at Ex.P19.
As per that, the claimant has spent Rs.72,000/- towards medical expenses of the deceased.
The said SCCH-23 MVC-6295/2023 bills have been meticulously examined and is found to be correct.
There is no contra evidence to disbelieve the genuineness of these bills.
Hence a sum of Rs.72,000/- is awarded under this head.

22. The calculation table stands as follows :
Compensation heads Compensation amount 1. Towards loss of dependency Rs.6,40,000/-
2 . Towards loss of Consortium to Rs. 48,400/- the petitioner No.1 3.
Towards loss to estate Rs. 18,150/-

4. Towards transportation of dead Rs. 18,150/-
body funeral and obsequies ceremony expenses 5.
Medical Expenses Rs. 72,000/-
23. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY :
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
24. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the RC owner and insured of Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-JW-5490 and SCCH-23 MVC-6295/2023 respondent No.3 being the insurer thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.3 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.
Hence issue No.3 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.

sentences.text: ISSUE NO.4 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.7,96,700/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.3 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
SCCH-23 MVC-6295/2023 On deposit of the award amount together with interest,
the claimant is entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :

Petitioner No.1 - 100% Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 a sum equal to 25% shall be deposited in her name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 75% shall be released to her through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said claimant is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on her deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
